name: Memucan
overview: Memucan was a male figure noted as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media, indicating a position of significant authority within the Persian empire. Beyond his role as a prince, Scripture does not provide additional tribal or familial details about him. His mention is concise, focusing primarily on his political status.
namesAndTitles: The name Memucan appears as a proper name in the biblical text without any specific meaning or divine origin provided. Therefore, it is simply recognized as his personal name as recorded in Esther 1:14.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Memucan beyond his identification as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media. No additional relational information is given.
scriptureSignificance: Memucan's significance lies in his role as one of the seven princes serving under the Persian king, highlighting the structured governance of the empire during the time of Esther. His mention underscores the political environment in which the events of Esther took place, reflecting the presence of influential advisors in the king's court.
